neighbours.label: 'from' in 'known from <evidence>': a species, text or thing attested only by named specimens, copies or sites (and anatomical 'is continued' as a weaker case), vs other uses of 'from'
fire: The giant penguin is known from a handful of leg bones dug up in New Zealand.
This early poem is known from two copies kept in a monastery library.
The beetle is known from only three specimens collected in 1902.
Much of the ancient play is known from quotations in later authors.
The extinct shark is known from its teeth, which are found worldwide.
The lost city is known from a few clay tablets and one inscription.
This orchid is known from a single valley in the northern Andes.
The composer's early sonata is known from a damaged manuscript in Vienna.
quiet: The giant penguin was dug up from a quarry in New Zealand.
This early poem was copied from an older book in the monastery library.
The beetle collector moved from Boston to Ohio in 1902.
Much of the ancient play was translated from Greek by later authors.
The extinct shark had teeth that were large and sharp.
The lost city was far from the coast, near a dry river.
This orchid grows in a single valley in the northern Andes.
The composer received a letter from his sister in Vienna.

predictions: 'known from' + specimens/manuscripts/sites 0.5-0.95; 'from' of origin, motion or source without 'known' under 0.1.
notes: Card: ' from' x10 in 'known from only a few observations', 'known from 21 manuscript copies', 'known from a Canadian fossil site'; ' continued' x5 in anatomy. Probe: known from a single partial skull 0.925, hymn known from three manuscripts 0.743, is continued forward 0.372, prolonged downward 0.237; was found as a skull 0.122, moved here from Ohio 0.015, meeting was continued 0.067.
